answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake tied to verifiable work history before transacting. To forge a new identity then costs real capital and time, since the stake must be earned through attested useful work rather than minted freely. Reputation acts like pigment in paint: it colors every transaction, and an agent that misbehaves stains its own stake, which is slashed. Honest agents climb toward the zenith of trust gradually, so mass-producing fake identities becomes economically irrational.
